The arguments of a model cardx fits: method.args

Source: R/ard_model_args.R
tfl_ard_model_args.Rd

cardx fits some models itself: ard_survival_survfit() the Kaplan-Meier estimate (survival::survfit()), ard_regression(), ard_emmeans_emmeans(), ard_emmeans_contrast() and ard_stats_anova() the model their method and package name ("glm", "coxph" of survival, "mmrm" of mmrm ...). The model's own arguments are written in method.args = list(...) of the analysis row's args: method.args = list(conf.type = "log-log") (the Kaplan-Meier interval SAS's PROC LIFETEST gives), method.args = list(ties = "breslow") (a Cox model as SAS's PROC PHREG fits it), method.args = list(family = binomial) (a logistic model), method.args = list(method = "Kenward-Roger") (MMRM's degrees of freedom), method.args = list(covariance = cov_struct("toep", visits = "AVISIT", subject = "USUBJID")) (MMRM's covariance when the formula has none), method = "glm.nb", package = "MASS" with method.args = list(link = log) (a negative binomial rate model: exacerbations, recurrent events) and method = "survreg", package = "survival" with method.args = list(dist = "lognormal") (a parametric survival model). The same arguments are the model's in a call written in x (ard_survival_survfit_diff(x = survival::survfit(..., conf.type = "log-log"))).

Usage

tfl_ard_model_args(method, package = "base")

Arguments

method

The model function: "survfit", "coxph", "glm", or "pkg::fun".

package

The package method is in, as cardx's package = ("base": the search path, stats then survival).

Value

A data frame, one row per argument the installed model function takes (formula, data, x, y and ... left out; those its ... reach after its own): fn, arg, default, kind, hint, choices, described (whether the catalog describes it). NULL when the function cannot be found.

Details

tfl_ard_spec() looks for each name in the installed model function (and where its ... go: survfit()'s survfitKM(), glm()'s and glm.nb()'s glm.control(), survreg()'s survreg.control(), coxph()'s coxph.control(), mmrm()'s mmrm_control()) and judges the values this catalog describes by their kind: conf.type = "loglog" would stop the program, tise = "breslow" too, and wieghts = W would be ignored by lm(); a covariance type mmrm does not have (cov_struct("un", ...), ~ un(AVISIT | USUBJID)), the visit column not in quotes, weights = "WTS" given to mmrm() (a vector, not a column name), link = logit of glm.nb() and init.theta = 0 too. formula and data are cardx's to give.

The catalog is inst/ard/model_args.csv (fn, arg, default, kind, hint, choices); a company adds rows with options(tflspec.ard_model_args = <data frame>).

Examples

tfl_ard_model_args("survfit", "survival")
#>                   fn        arg default     kind
#> 1  survival::survfit    weights    <NA> variable
#> 2  survival::survfit     subset    <NA>     code
#> 3  survival::survfit  na.action    <NA>     code
#> 4  survival::survfit      stype       1   choice
#> 5  survival::survfit      ctype       1   choice
#> 6  survival::survfit         id    <NA> variable
#> 7  survival::survfit    cluster    <NA> variable
#> 8  survival::survfit     robust    <NA>  logical
#> 9  survival::survfit     istate    <NA>     code
#> 10 survival::survfit    timefix    TRUE  logical
#> 11 survival::survfit      etype    <NA>     code
#> 12 survival::survfit      model   FALSE  logical
#> 13 survival::survfit      error    <NA>     code
#> 14 survival::survfit      entry   FALSE  logical
#> 15 survival::survfit      time0   FALSE  logical
#> 16 survival::survfit     se.fit    TRUE  logical
#> 17 survival::survfit   conf.int    0.95   number
#> 18 survival::survfit  conf.type     log   choice
#> 19 survival::survfit conf.lower   usual   choice
#> 20 survival::survfit start.time    <NA>   number
#> 21 survival::survfit  influence   FALSE  logical
#> 22 survival::survfit       type    <NA>     code
#>                                                                                                                            hint
#> 1                                                                      Case weights: a column of the data, not in quotes (WTS).
#> 2                                                                                                                              
#> 3                                                                                                                              
#> 4                                   How survival is estimated: 1 the Kaplan-Meier product (default), 2 exp(-cumulative hazard).
#> 5                           The cumulative hazard: 1 Nelson-Aalen (default), 2 with the Fleming-Harrington correction for ties.
#> 6                                                 The subject column, not in quotes (USUBJID), when a subject has several rows.
#> 7                                                 The cluster of the robust standard errors: a column, not in quotes (USUBJID).
#> 8                                                      TRUE: robust (infinitesimal jackknife) standard errors of the estimates.
#> 9                                                                                                                              
#> 10                                                        TRUE (default): times that differ only by rounding are taken as tied.
#> 11                                                                                                                             
#> 12                                                                                                                             
#> 13                                                                                                                             
#> 14                                                                                                                             
#> 15                                                                                                                             
#> 16                                                     TRUE (default): the standard errors, and so the intervals, are computed.
#> 17                                           Confidence level of the Kaplan-Meier estimates' intervals, between 0 and 1 (0.95).
#> 18 How the interval is computed: log (survival's default), log-log (SAS PROC LIFETEST's default), plain, logit, arcsin or none.
#> 19                                        The lower limit's standard error: usual (default), peto or modified (Dorey and Korn).
